cevap: U. S. Steel (CIK 0001163302) discusses the Nippon Steel deal as a pending, contested merger rather than a closed transaction. Per the FY2024 10-K (accession 0001163302-25-000018, filed 31 Jan 2025) and the Q1 2025 10-Q (accession 0001163302-25-000030, filed 2 May 2025): the Merger Agreement was signed 18 December 2023 with Nippon Steel North America, Inc. (Purchaser), 2023 Merger Subsidiary, Inc. and Nippon Steel Corporation; each U. S. Steel share converts into the right to receive $55.00 in cash, and the company would survive as a wholly owned subsidiary of Purchaser. Stockholders approved on 12 April 2024 with 98.8% of shares voted. HSR waiting period has expired and all non-U.S. regulatory approvals were obtained, leaving CFIUS clearance as the outstanding condition. After CFIUS referred the matter, President Biden issued an order on 3 January 2025 prohibiting the merger and requiring the parties to abandon it within thirty days; on 10 January 2025 CFIUS extended that deadline to 18 June 2025. On 6 January 2025 U. S. Steel, NSC and Purchaser sued in the D.C. Circuit challenging the President's order and the CFIUS process as politically motivated and unconstitutional, and separately sued Cleveland-Cliffs, its CEO Lourenco Goncalves and USW president David McCall in the Western District of Pennsylvania for alleged anticompetitive/racketeering conduct; motions to dismiss were argued 12 March 2025 and remained pending. On 6 April 2025 the President issued a Presidential Memorandum directing CFIUS to conduct a de novo review with a recommendation due 21 May 2025, and the D.C. Circuit granted a 60-day abeyance of the litigation on 11 April 2025. As to business operations, the company states the Merger Agreement requires it to operate in the ordinary course and restricts it, without Purchaser's consent, from taking specified actions outside the ordinary course until closing or termination; its forward-looking-statement disclosures flag risks from transaction-related litigation, inability to satisfy closing conditions, and disruption of management time from ongoing business operations due to the proposed transaction. Meanwhile the underlying business continued to be run and invested in (e.g. Big River Steel 2 produced its first coil in October 2024, lifting Mini Mill capability from 3.3 to 6.3 million tons).

On the basis of what was on file with the SEC by 16 May 2025, Amazon appears to be the biggest 2025 capex spender, but only Meta gives an explicit full-year dollar plan. Meta's Q1 2025 10-Q (accession 0001326801-25-000054) states: 'We anticipate making capital expenditures of approximately $64 billion to $72 billion in 2025 to support our core business and generative AI efforts'; Meta's Q1 2025 capex including finance-lease principal was $13.69 billion. Alphabet's Q1 2025 10-Q (accession 0001652044-25-000043) reports $17.2 billion of capex in Q1 2025 versus $12.0 billion in Q1 2024 and says only that it expects to increase its technical-infrastructure investment relative to 2024 in support of AI; no dollar guidance appears in the 10-Q or in the FY2024 10-K (accession 0001652044-25-000014). Amazon's Q1 2025 10-Q (accession 0001018724-25-000036) reports cash capital expenditures of $24.3 billion in Q1 2025 versus $13.9 billion in Q1 2024 and says it expects cash capex to increase in 2025, driven primarily by technology infrastructure, again without a dollar figure. Comparing the only like-for-like data in the filings, Amazon's Q1 run rate (~$97 billion annualized) is above Meta's guided $64-72 billion and roughly $10 billion above Alphabet's much larger Q1 spend gap, so Amazon plans to spend the most, with Alphabet second and Meta third. Note that the exact Alphabet and Amazon full-year 2025 targets were given on earnings calls rather than in SEC filings, so they cannot be sourced with these tools.

KKR & Co. Inc. priced 6.25% Series D Mandatory Convertible Preferred Stock on 4-5 March 2025 (pricing term sheet FWP, accession 0001140361-25-007061; closing 8-K accession 0001140361-25-007608). Size: upsized from an announced 30,000,000 shares to 45,000,000 shares, plus a 6,750,000-share over-allotment option that the underwriters exercised in full, so 51,750,000 shares, or $2,587,500,000 aggregate liquidation preference, were issued. Trade date 5 March 2025; settlement/closing 7 March 2025, the same day KKR filed the Certificate of Designations in Delaware. Price: $50.00 per share public offering price with a $1.125 per share underwriting discount; net proceeds were approximately $2.53 billion. Liquidation preference: $50.00 per share plus accumulated and unpaid dividends, ranking ahead of common stock and behind debt and senior stock. Dividends: 6.25% per annum on the $50.00 liquidation preference, cumulative and payable when, as and if declared, in cash or (subject to limits) in common stock or a combination; quarterly on 1 March, 1 June, 1 September and 1 December through 1 March 2028, first payment 1 June 2025 of approximately $0.7292 per share and $0.78125 per share thereafter; record dates 15 Feb/May/Aug/Nov. While the preferred is outstanding, no common dividends or buybacks may occur unless all accumulated preferred dividends have been paid or set aside, and parity stock dividends must be paid pro rata. Conversion: mandatory conversion expected 1 March 2028 at between 0.3312 (minimum) and 0.4140 (maximum) common shares per preferred share, based on the 20-trading-day VWAP ending near 1 March 2028; initial price approximately $120.7729, threshold appreciation price approximately $150.9662 (about 25% above the initial price), floor price $42.2705. Holders may convert early at any time at the minimum rate of 0.3312 shares; on a fundamental change they may convert at a fundamental change conversion rate (table ranging 0.3280-0.4140) plus a fundamental change dividend make-whole amount discounted at 4.77% and any accumulated dividend amount. Listed on NYSE as 'KKR PR D' (CUSIP 48251W 500). Purpose: KKR said it intends to use net proceeds to acquire additional equity interests in core private equity portfolio companies reported in its Strategic Holdings segment and for other general corporate purposes. Voting rights: the 8-K states that the Certificate of Designations establishes the voting rights of the preferred but the 8-K and pricing term sheet I read do not summarize them; the detail sits in Exhibit 3.1 to accession 0001140361-25-007608, which I did not read within budget.

Shift4 Payments' FY2024 10-K (accession 0001794669-25-000011, fiscal year ended 31 December 2024) discloses vendor concentration in two places. In the Concentration Risk accounting note: 'The Company's merchant processing activity in North America is facilitated by one vendor,' with management stating it believes that vendor maintains appropriate backup systems and alternative arrangements to avoid a significant processing disruption. The same note adds a related dependency: because Shift4 is not a member bank in North America, it processes card transactions through a sponsorship agreement with a member bank, and if Shift4 breached that agreement the sponsor could terminate it, leaving Shift4 180 days to find an alternative bank sponsor. The risk factor 'Because we rely on third-party vendors to provide products and services, we could be adversely impacted if they fail to fulfill their obligations' expands on this: in the U.S., EU and Canada Shift4 is dependent on its relationship with a single third-party processor for merchant authorization, processing, risk and chargeback monitoring, accounting, and clearing and settlement; there is no assurance backup systems would avoid a significant disruption, and if the processor agreement were terminated or could not be renewed on favorable terms it may be difficult to replace those services. Shift4 also relies on third parties for specific software and devices, notes those providers serve competitors too, and states it does not have long-term or exclusive contracts with them. Consequences flagged include loss of revenue, loss of merchants and software partners, data loss, card-network fines, regulatory action, reputational harm, fraud losses, and added operating and development costs. The filing does not quantify the vendor concentration as a percentage of purchases or costs.

Microsoft's FY2024 10-K (accession 0000950170-24-087843, fiscal year ended 30 June 2024) states that as of June 30, 2024 it employed approximately 228,000 people on a full-time basis, 126,000 in the U.S. and 102,000 internationally. So the share located outside the United States is 102,000 / 228,000 = approximately 44.7% (about 45%), with the remaining 126,000 / 228,000 = approximately 55.3% in the U.S.

Roughly $467 million. Basis (Dutch Bros FY2024 XBRL as reported in its FY2024 10-K filed 13 February 2025): revenue $1,281.0 million and cost of sales (us-gaap:CostOfGoodsAndServicesSold) $940.9 million, giving 2024 gross profit of $340.1 million and a gross margin of 26.55%. Applying a 30% revenue CAGR for two years: $1,281.0m x 1.30^2 = $2,164.9 million of 2026 revenue. Compressing the gross margin by 500 basis points: 26.55% - 5.00% = 21.55%. 2026 gross profit = $2,164.9m x 21.55% = $466.6 million, i.e. approximately $467 million (about $2,165 million revenue less about $1,698 million cost of sales). Note that Dutch Bros does not report a us-gaap GrossProfit tag; this uses its reported cost of sales line, which for its company-operated shops includes beverage/food/packaging, labor and occupancy costs.

Redfin (NASDAQ: RDFN, CIK 0001382821) agreed on 9-10 March 2025 to be acquired by Rocket Companies (NYSE: RKT) in an all-stock transaction. Per the joint announcement filed as Exhibit 99.1 to Rocket's 8-K (accession 0000950142-25-000696, filed 10 March 2025; also filed by Redfin as accession 0001628280-25-011457 / Form 425 accession 0000950142-25-000697): the price was $12.50 per Redfin share, or $1.75 billion of equity value. Each Redfin share is to be exchanged for a fixed ratio of 0.7926 shares of Rocket Companies Class A common stock, a 63% premium to Redfin's 30-day VWAP ending 7 March 2025. Rocket said it expects more than $200 million of run-rate synergies by 2027 (about $140 million cost, more than $60 million revenue) and accretion to adjusted EPS by end-2026. The filings I read do not disclose an enterprise value for the transaction - the press release quotes only the per-share price and the $1.75 billion equity value - so I could not source an enterprise value figure with these tools.

Floor & Decor's comparable store sales decreased 0.8% in the fourth quarter of fiscal 2024 (the quarter ended 26 December 2024). Source: the Q4/FY2024 earnings release filed as Exhibit 99.1 to its 8-K, accession 0001507079-25-000012, filed 20 February 2025. For context in the same release, Q4 net sales were $1,107.4 million, up 5.7% from $1,048.1 million a year earlier, diluted EPS was $0.44, operating income was $59.2 million (up 28.3%), and 10 new warehouse stores opened, ending at 251 warehouse stores and five design studios. Full-year fiscal 2024 comparable store sales fell 7.1% on net sales of $4,455.8 million, and the company guided fiscal 2025 comps to approximately flat to +3.0%.

Per Zillow Group's FY2024 10-K (accession 0001617640-25-000016, filed 11 February 2025), the acquisitions of the prior two years were all completed in 2023 and were tuck-in purchases of software and transaction-services capability rather than balance-sheet-heavy home buying: Aryeo, a software company serving real estate photographers, on 31 July 2023 for about $35 million total ($15 million cash net of cash acquired plus 380,259 Class C shares valued at $20 million); substantially all assets and liabilities of Spruce, a tech-enabled title and escrow platform, on 11 September 2023 for about $19 million cash; and Follow Up Boss, a CRM for real estate professionals, on 8 December 2023 for $399 million cash net of cash acquired plus contingent consideration of up to $100 million over three years (total purchase price $484 million, of which $402 million goodwill and $86 million intangibles - developed technology $50 million, customer relationships $34 million, trade names $2 million). Zillow explicitly frames the Follow Up Boss deal as 'consistent with our strategy to invest in a more integrated software experience for our customers.' No material business combinations are disclosed for 2024, so the strategy in the period was to digest the 2023 software/services acquisitions rather than to keep buying. This lines up with the revenue mix disclosed in Note 17: total revenue of $2,236 million in 2024 versus $1,945 million in 2023 and $1,958 million in 2022, split as Residential $1,594 million (71% of revenue, up 10%), Mortgages $145 million (6%, up 51%), Rentals $453 million (20%, up 27%) and Other $44 million (2%). The fastest-growing lines are exactly the ones the acquisitions feed: Follow Up Boss and Aryeo deepen the agent software/listing-media layer that supports Premier Agent and the enhanced-market Residential business, while Spruce brings title and escrow in-house to capture more of the adjacent transaction economics alongside the mortgage originations business. In other words, the acquisitions push Zillow further from a pure advertising-marketplace revenue base toward integrated software plus transaction services, matching the shift in mix toward Rentals and Mortgages, which together went from about 23% of revenue in 2023 to about 27% in 2024.
